plan.goal: Read tests\slugify.rs to understand the expected input/output behavior of the slugify function.
plan.result:
Read tests\slugify.rs and confirmed the expected behavior of the slugify function:

- Case 1: slugify("Hello, Marix World!") → "hello-marix-world"
- Case 2: slugify("rust___agents   work") → "rust-agents-work"
- Case 3: slugify("---Ship It---") → "ship-it"
- Case 4: slugify(" MX 42 ") → "mx-42"

From these cases, slugify should lowercase input, replace runs of non-alphanumeric characters with hyphens, and strip leading/trailing hyphens.

plan.goal: Inspect src\lib.rs to see the current implementation of slugify.
plan.result:
Inspected src\lib.rs. The current implementation of slugify is:

`pub fn slugify(input: &str) -> String` which trims input, maps each character: if `ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric()` it lowercases with `ch.to_ascii_lowercase()`, otherwise it emits a hyphen `'-'`, then collects into a String.

This implementation does not collapse consecutive non-alphanumeric characters into a single hyphen nor strip leading/trailing hyphens, so it would produce e.g. "hello--marix--world" for "Hello, Marix World!", failing the expected test outputs.
